title: Big Spending, Big Doubts: Why Meta's Bill Shook the Nasdaq
body:
What rattled Wall Street on Thursday was not a sales miss but a question about money that has already been spent. Meta, whose revenue of $64.6 billion beat forecasts, still fell about 7% after its free cash flow (잉여현금흐름) turned negative and it lifted the low end of its **capex** range to $135–145 billion. Investors who had cheered heavy AI investment for months suddenly grew **skeptical** about when, or whether, that spending will pay off. As a result, the Nasdaq slid 2.6% to 26,008.86, while the S&P 500 lost a milder 1.2%.

One of the clearest warning signs was the VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge (공포 지수), which jumped about 14% to 19.03. At the same time, the 10-year Treasury yield fell from 5.15% to 4.95% as cautious money moved into **safe-haven** bonds. Most of the selling, however, was concentrated in big tech: small-cap stocks actually edged up 0.1%, which suggests that investors were doubting a single story rather than the whole economy. Even so, the **jittery** mood is likely to **spill over into** Asia. Having already dropped 3.5% to 5,533.77 on Thursday, the KOSPI, which is heavily tied to chipmakers, remains sensitive to any doubt about AI, and oil near $99 a barrel could **weigh on** it further. Although one bad session does not **undermine** the long-term case for AI by itself, such swings are unlikely to fade unless the profits finally show up.
ko:
목요일 월가를 뒤흔든 것은 매출 부진이 아니라 이미 써버린 돈에 대한 의문이었다. 메타는 매출 646억 달러로 예상치를 넘었지만, 잉여현금흐름이 마이너스로 돌아서고 설비투자(capex) 범위 하단을 1,350억~1,450억 달러로 올리자 주가가 약 7% 떨어졌다. 몇 달 동안 대규모 AI 투자에 환호하던 투자자들이 갑자기 그 지출이 언제, 아니 과연 성과를 낼지 의심하기 시작한 것이다. 그 결과 나스닥은 2.6% 내린 26,008.86으로 밀렸고, S&P 500은 그보다 완만한 1.2% 하락에 그쳤다.

가장 뚜렷한 경고 신호 중 하나는 월가의 '공포 지수' VIX로, 약 14% 뛰어 19.03이 됐다. 동시에 조심스러운 자금이 안전자산인 채권으로 옮겨 가면서 미 10년물 국채 금리는 5.15%에서 4.95%로 내려왔다. 다만 매도의 대부분은 대형 기술주에 몰렸다. 소형주는 오히려 0.1% 올랐는데, 이는 투자자들이 경제 전체가 아니라 한 가지 스토리(AI)를 의심하고 있었다는 뜻이다. 그렇다 해도 이 불안한 분위기는 아시아로 번질 가능성이 크다. 이미 목요일에 3.5% 떨어져 5,533.77로 마감한 코스피는 반도체 비중이 커서 AI에 대한 작은 의심에도 민감하고, 배럴당 99달러 근처의 유가도 추가 부담이 될 수 있다. 하루의 급락만으로 AI의 장기 논리가 무너지지는 않지만, 이익이 실제로 나타나지 않는 한 이런 출렁임은 쉽게 사라지지 않을 것이다.

vocab.ko: 설비투자(공장·데이터센터 등 장기 자산에 쓰는 돈)
vocab.en_easy: Money a company spends on long-term things like buildings, machines, or data centers.
vocab.ex: Investors got nervous when the company said its capex would double next year.

vocab.en_easy: An investment people buy when they are scared, because it usually keeps its value.
vocab.ex: When stocks fall hard, money often flows into safe-haven assets like Treasuries and gold.

vocab.en_easy: Nervous and worried, so you react quickly to small bad news.
vocab.ex: I always get a little jittery right before my OPIc recording starts.

vocab.en_easy: Not easily believing that something is true or will work.
vocab.ex: I was skeptical about running apps at first, but now I use one every day.

vocab.en_easy: To make something weaker or less likely to succeed, often slowly.
vocab.ex: Staying up late every night can really undermine your progress at the gym.

vocab.en_easy: When a problem or feeling in one place spreads to another place.
vocab.ex: Stress from work sometimes spills over into my weekends, so I go jogging to reset.

vocab.en_easy: To put pressure on something or someone and make it go down or feel worse.
vocab.ex: Higher oil prices continue to weigh on airline stocks.

grammar.point: 관계대명사 what (= the thing that, 명사절)
grammar.quote: What rattled Wall Street on Thursday was not a sales miss but a question about money that has already been spent.
grammar.explain_ko: what은 선행사를 품은 관계대명사라 앞에 명사가 없다(= the thing that). 'What rattled Wall Street'가 통째로 주어(명사절)이고, 명사절 주어는 단수 취급 → was. 수능 어법 단골: 앞에 선행사가 있으면 which/that, 없으면 what. 'The thing what ~'(X), 'That rattled Wall Street was ~'(X — that은 선행사 필요).
examples: What surprised me most was how quickly the stock bounced back.
What I love most about my gym is that it's never too crowded in the morning. (OPIc 묘사 — 첫 문장을 이걸로 열면 IH 느낌)

grammar.quote: One of the clearest warning signs was the VIX… / Most of the selling, however, was concentrated in big tech…
grammar.explain_ko: ① 'one of + 복수명사'의 진짜 주어는 one → 단수 동사(was). signs에 끌려 were 쓰면 틀림. ② 부분표현(most·some·half·the rest·분수 + of + 명사)은 of 뒤 명사에 동사를 맞춘다: the selling(불가산) → was, most of the stocks(복수) → were. 수능 어법에서 주어와 동사 사이에 수식어(however, of 구)가 끼면 거리를 두고 확인.
examples: Half of the investors were selling, but most of the money was going into bonds.
One of the reasons I like jogging is that I don't need any equipment. (OPIc 루틴·이유)

tense.sentence: …a question about money that has already been spent.
tense.why_ko: 돈을 쓴 건 과거지만 '이미 써버려서 지금 되돌릴 수 없다'는 현재 결과가 핵심이라 현재완료. 돈은 '쓰이는' 대상이라 수동태(been spent).

tense.sentence: Investors who had cheered heavy AI investment for months suddenly grew skeptical…
tense.why_ko: '의심하게 된(grew)' 시점보다 더 앞에서부터 몇 달간 환호해 왔으므로 had cheered. for months(기간)와 함께 '그 시점까지 계속'을 나타낸다.

review.q: With the earnings report coming out tomorrow, I'm going to ______ buying more shares until I see the actual numbers.
review.exp_ko: hold off on ~ing = (당분간) ~을 미루다. 'until I see the numbers'(숫자를 볼 때까지)가 단서 — 지금은 안 산다는 뜻. follow through on(계획을 끝까지 실행하다)은 'until'과 논리가 반대, catch up on(밀린 것을 따라잡다)·keep up with(뒤처지지 않고 따라가다)는 '매수를 미룬다'는 의미가 안 된다.

review.q: 'The rally lacked breadth: only a handful of giant tech stocks actually went up.' 에서 breadth와 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: how far an index rises in a single trading day
how much money changes hands during a session
how long a trend lasts before it finally reverses
how many different stocks take part in a market move
review.exp_ko: breadth(시장 폭) = 상승·하락에 '얼마나 많은 종목이' 참여했나. 뒤의 'only a handful of stocks'(소수 종목만)가 단서. ①은 상승 폭(magnitude), ②는 거래대금(volume), ③은 추세 지속 기간(duration) — 모두 시장 지표지만 '참여 종목 수'와는 다르다.

review.q: The first big earnings report of the week often ______ for the rest of the market, so traders watch it closely.
review.exp_ko: set the tone (for ~) = (~의) 분위기를 정하다. 'for the rest of the market'과 짝을 이루는 연어. take the lead(선두에 서다)는 for the rest와 어울리지 않고, make the cut(기준을 통과하다)·hold the line(버티다, 현 수준을 지키다)은 '나머지 시장의 분위기'라는 의미가 안 나온다.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Having already dropped 3.5% to 5,533.77 on Thursday, the KOSPI remains sensitive to any doubt about AI, and oil near $99 a barrel could ______ it further."
quiz.exp_ko: 이미 떨어진 코스피에 비싼 유가가 '추가로 부담을 줄' 수 있다 = weigh on. further(더)와 '하락' 문맥이 단서. bear on(~와 관련되다)은 '관련'만 있지 하락 압력이 없고, build on(~을 발판으로 삼다)은 긍정 의미, take on(떠맡다·맞서다)은 유가가 주어로 어색하다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"One of the clearest warning signs (A)were the VIX, (B)which jumped about 14% to 19.03. (C)What rattled investors was a question about money (D)that has already been spent."
quiz.exp_ko: 'One of + 복수명사'의 주어는 one → was가 맞다(A 틀림). (B) which는 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법으로 the VIX를 받아 맞고, (C) What은 선행사 없이 명사절 주어를 이끌어 맞으며(That이면 틀림), (D) that은 선행사 money를 받는 관계대명사로 맞다.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Rising oil prices were the main reason the Nasdaq fell more sharply than the S&P 500.
Investors abandoned stocks across the board and moved most of their money into bonds.
Meta's results proved that the long-term case for AI has been seriously damaged.
Strong revenue alone could not calm investors who now want proof that AI spending will pay off.
quiz.exp_ko: 첫 문장(매출이 아니라 이미 쓴 돈에 대한 의문)과 마지막 문장(이익이 나오지 않는 한 출렁임 지속)이 주제문 → ④. ①유가는 부수 요인으로만 등장, ②소형주는 오히려 0.1% 올라 '전반적 이탈'이 아님, ③본문은 하루로 장기 논리가 훼손되지 않는다(does not undermine)고 했다 — 정반대.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 숫자로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: The 10-year Treasury yield fell by about 2 percentage points during the session.
In percentage terms, the Nasdaq fell more than twice as much as the S&P 500.
The VIX's percentage rise was less than five points larger than the KOSPI's drop.
Small-cap stocks declined, though by less than the S&P 500 did.
quiz.exp_ko: 나스닥 2.6% ÷ S&P 1.2% ≈ 2.2배 → '2배 넘게' ②가 맞다. ①5.15%→4.95%는 0.2%p 하락(2%p 아님 — %p 단위 함정), ③VIX +14% vs 코스피 −3.5% → 차이 약 10.5포인트(5 미만 아님), ④소형주는 0.1% '상승'(edged up)이라 방향이 틀렸다.

talk.topic: Big spending, big doubts — 메타는 실적이 좋았는데 왜 7% 빠졌나
talk.setting_ko: 금요일 아침 출근길 지하철. 미국 주식 하는 회사 동료 A와 B가 밤사이 나스닥 급락 얘기를 한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see the Nasdaq last night? Down 2.6%. My app was a sea of red.
dialogue.ko: 어젯밤 나스닥 봤어? 2.6% 빠졌어. 앱이 온통 하락 색깔이더라(미국식 a sea of red = 한국 앱의 파란색).

dialogue.en: Yeah, it was Meta, mostly. Their revenue actually beat, but the stock still dropped like 7%.
dialogue.ko: 응, 거의 메타 때문이야. 매출은 오히려 예상보다 좋았는데 주가는 7%쯤 떨어졌어.

dialogue.en: Wait, how does that work? Good numbers, bad reaction?
dialogue.ko: 잠깐, 그게 어떻게 돼? 숫자는 좋은데 반응은 나쁘다고?

dialogue.en: They're burning through cash on AI. Free cash flow went negative, and people want to know when all that spending will pay off.
dialogue.ko: AI에 현금을 엄청 태우고 있거든. 잉여현금흐름이 마이너스가 됐고, 사람들은 그 돈이 언제 성과를 낼지 알고 싶어 해.

dialogue.en: So it's kind of a wake-up call for the whole AI trade.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 AI 투자 전체에 대한 일종의 경고등이네.

dialogue.en: Maybe. But I'd take the panic with a grain of salt. Small caps were actually up.
dialogue.ko: 그럴 수도. 근데 이 공포는 좀 걸러서 들을래. 소형주는 오히려 올랐거든.

dialogue.en: Good point. I'm not selling anything today — I'll just wait and see what Korea does.
dialogue.ko: 맞네. 오늘은 아무것도 안 팔래. 한국장이 어떻게 하는지 일단 지켜볼게.

dialogue.en: Smart. Let's talk again at lunch.

expressions.when_ko: 돈·시간을 들인 일이 결국 좋은 결과로 돌아올 때
expressions.ex: All those early morning workouts finally paid off — I ran my best 10K.

expressions.when_ko: 회사·사람이 현금이나 자원을 너무 빨리 소진할 때
expressions.ex: I burned through my whole travel budget in the first three days.

expressions.when_ko: 문제를 깨닫게 해 주는 사건을 말할 때
expressions.ex: Losing 10% in one week was a real wake-up call for me.

expressions.en: take ~ with a grain of salt
expressions.when_ko: 뉴스·소문·예측을 너무 믿지 말라고 할 때
expressions.ex: I take most stock tips on YouTube with a grain of salt.

expressions.when_ko: 바로 행동하지 않고 결과를 기다릴 때
expressions.ex: I'm not sure if I'll travel this winter. I'll just wait and see.

your_turn.q_en: If a company you invested in posted good sales but its stock still fell, what would you do?
your_turn.hint_ko: 매출 좋은데 주가 하락 → 이유 확인(비용·현금흐름) → 내 행동(지켜보기/분할매수) → 이유 한 줄. take ~ with a grain of salt, wait and see 써보기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I'd try not to panic. First, I'd check why it fell — maybe the company is burning through cash or its outlook was weak. If the long-term story still makes sense, I'd just wait and see for a few days instead of selling right away. I'd also take the scary headlines with a grain of salt, because one bad day doesn't always mean the investment won't pay off.

talk.topic: 콘서트 티켓팅 실패 — 친구와 대안 찾기 (음악 감상)
talk.setting_ko: 금요일 저녁, 좋아하는 밴드 내한 공연 티켓팅에 실패한 A가 친구 B에게 전화한다. (서베이 #23 음악 감상)

dialogue.en: Ugh, I didn't get the tickets. The whole show was sold out in like three minutes.
dialogue.ko: 으, 티켓 못 구했어. 공연 전체가 3분 만에 매진됐어.

dialogue.en: No way. You've had their new album on repeat all month!
dialogue.ko: 말도 안 돼. 너 한 달 내내 걔네 새 앨범만 반복해서 들었잖아!

dialogue.en: I know. I was really into this tour, too. I even took the afternoon off.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 이번 투어 진짜 기대했는데. 오후 반차까지 냈다니까.

dialogue.en: Hey, it's not the end of the world. They might add a second date.
dialogue.ko: 야, 세상 끝난 거 아니야. 공연 하루 더 추가할 수도 있잖아.

dialogue.en: True. And if they do, I'm setting three alarms this time.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 추가되면 이번엔 알람 세 개 맞춰 놓을 거야.

dialogue.en: In the meantime, there's an indie gig at a small club in Hongdae tomorrow. Wanna go?
dialogue.ko: 그동안 내일 홍대 작은 클럽에서 인디 공연 있는데, 갈래?

dialogue.en: Honestly? That sounds great. Count me in.
Cool. I'll send you the link.

expressions.ex: The early-morning running class is always sold out by Monday.

expressions.when_ko: 한 노래·앨범에 꽂혀 계속 들을 때 (OPIc 음악 감상 필수)
expressions.ex: I've had this song on repeat during my workouts all week.
These days I'm really into old K-pop from the 2000s.

expressions.en: It's not the end of the world.
expressions.ko: 세상 끝난 거 아니야 / 큰일 아니야
expressions.when_ko: 실망한 사람을 위로하거나 내 실수를 가볍게 넘길 때
expressions.ex: I missed my workout today, but it's not the end of the world.
A hike this Saturday? Count me in.

your_turn.q_en: Tell me about a time you really wanted to see a concert or performance. What happened?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거 경험: 누구 공연·왜 가고 싶었는지 → 티켓 과정(성공/실패) → 결과·감정 → 지금 생각. 과거시제 유지, have ~ on repeat · It's not the end of the world 써보기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, a couple of years ago, I really wanted to see a band I was really into at the time. I had their album on repeat for months, so when the tour was announced, I set alarms and logged in early. But the show was sold out in about five minutes, and I was so disappointed. A friend told me it wasn't the end of the world, and actually, she was right — they added a second date a week later, and I finally got tickets. The concert was amazing, and I still listen to that album when I go jogging.

opic.survey_topic: 금요일 — 셀프 소개 + 주간 복습 콤보 (카페/커피전문점 #12 · 조깅 #46 · 공원 가기 #6)

combo.q_en: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.
combo.q_ko: 이제 인터뷰를 시작하겠습니다. 자신에 대해 조금 이야기해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(이름 대신 '사는 곳·하는 일' 한 줄) → 본문 ① 평일 모습(일·출퇴근) ② 퇴근 후·주말 취미 2개(헬스·조깅/카페) — 서베이 주제를 미리 깔아 두기 ③ 요즘 관심사(주식 공부·영어) → 마무리(어떤 사람인지 한 줄). 실제 시험에서 채점 안 된다는 말도 있지만 첫인상·워밍업이라 60~90초로 짧고 매끄럽게. 모범답안의 직업·동네는 본인 정보로 바꿔서 외우기. IH/AL 포인트: 현재·현재완료 섞기, 디테일(시간·장소), 필러 1~2회.
combo.model_answer: Okay, so, I'm in my late twenties, and I live in Seoul — in a pretty quiet neighborhood near a big park. I work at a company downtown, so on weekdays my life is kind of simple: I commute by subway, work until about six, and then head straight to the gym. To be more specific, I lift weights three or four times a week, and on the other days I go jogging in the park near my place. I've been doing that for a few years now, and it's become a big part of who I am. On weekends, I usually grab a coffee at a café I like and just relax with some music. Oh, and lately I've gotten into investing, so I've been reading market news every morning, which is also how I practice my English. I mean, it's tough sometimes, but I enjoy learning new things. So yeah, I'd describe myself as someone who likes routines but is always trying to get a little better. That's pretty much it about me.

key_phrases.en: It's become a big part of who I am.
key_phrases.ko: 그게 제 삶의 큰 부분이 됐어요

key_phrases.en: I'd describe myself as someone who ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '이름·나이·직업' 나열로 끝나고, IH는 '평일→주말→요즘'처럼 시간 흐름으로 묶으며, AL은 마지막에 '나는 어떤 사람'이라는 정리 문장으로 문단을 닫는다.

combo.q_en: In your background survey, you indicated that you go to coffee shops. What do you usually do when you go to a coffee shop? Tell me about your typical routine, from the moment you walk in until you leave.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 커피전문점에 간다고 하셨는데요. 커피숍에 가면 보통 무엇을 하나요? 들어가는 순간부터 나올 때까지의 전형적인 루틴을 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·얼마나 자주·어디) → 본문 ① 들어가서 주문(메뉴·이유) ② 자리 잡고 하는 일(음악·책·주식 뉴스) ③ 작은 습관·디테일(늘 앉는 자리, 리필) → 마무리(카페 시간이 나에게 주는 의미). 루틴이므로 현재시제 일관(usually, always, tend to), 순서 연결어(first, once ~, after that, by the time). 10/21 카페 talk 표현(It's packed, Is this seat taken?) 재활용 = 주간 복습.
combo.model_answer: Well, I usually go to a café on Saturday mornings — there's a small one about ten minutes from my place. So, once I walk in, the first thing I do is check if my favorite seat is free. It's this corner table by the window, and honestly, if it's taken, my whole mood changes a little. Anyway, I order an iced Americano, even in winter — I know, I know, it's a Korean thing. While I'm waiting, I chat with the barista for a minute because we kind of know each other now. After that, I sit down, put my earphones in, and play some lo-fi music. Then I either read a book or catch up on the market news from the week. Actually, I tend to write down a few English expressions I find, too. By the time I finish my coffee, it's usually been about two hours. What I like most about this routine is that it's the only time I'm not in a rush, so it kind of recharges me for the next week.

key_phrases.en: The first thing I do is ~
I know, I know, it's a Korean thing.
key_phrases.ko: 알아요, 알아요, 한국 사람 특징이죠 (자연스러운 자기수정·유머)

key_phrases.en: By the time I ~, it's usually been ~

combo.level_up_ko: 루틴 문제에서 IH는 순서 연결어로 흐름을 만들고, AL은 '루틴이 깨지는 순간'(자리 뺏기면 기분 변함) 같은 작은 예외 디테일로 생생함을 더한다.

combo.q_en: You also said that you go jogging. Tell me about a memorable experience you had while jogging. When was it, where were you, and what happened? Please tell me the story in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 조깅도 한다고 하셨죠. 조깅하다가 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 언제, 어디서, 무슨 일이 있었나요? 가능한 한 자세히 이야기해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디 — 배경 한 줄) → 본문 ① 평소와 같던 시작 ② 사건(갑작스러운 비·부상·사람과의 만남) ③ 어떻게 대처했고 어떤 감정이었는지 → 마무리(그 뒤로 바뀐 점). 과거시제 일관 + 배경은 과거진행(was running) — 시제 섞임이 IH/AL 채점 핵심. 10/22 공원 러닝 talk(pace yourself, totally winded) 표현 재활용. 근육 이름(calves, hamstrings)으로 구체화.
combo.model_answer: Oh, I remember one really clearly. It was last summer, maybe in July, and I was jogging along the river in the park near my place after work. Everything was normal at first — I was listening to music and keeping a nice, easy pace. But about halfway through, the sky suddenly turned dark, and it started pouring. I mean, really pouring. I didn't have anywhere to hide, so I just kept running. Then, to make things worse, I felt my left calf tighten up — I think I hadn't stretched enough that day. So I had to stop and limp to a bridge to get out of the rain. While I was standing there, completely soaked, an older guy from a running crew stopped and showed me how to stretch my calf and hamstrings properly. We ended up talking for almost twenty minutes. Long story short, I joined that crew a few weeks later. Looking back, it was a terrible run, but it turned into a really good memory, and now I never skip my warm-up.

key_phrases.en: It turned into a really good memory.

combo.level_up_ko: 과거 경험에서 IM은 과거형 사건 나열, IH는 '배경(과거진행)→사건(과거)→원인(과거완료 hadn't stretched)'으로 시제를 섞고, AL은 'Looking back'으로 현재 시점의 의미까지 연결해 마무리한다.

useful.when_ko: 일반적인 말 뒤에 디테일(숫자·장소·근육 이름)을 붙일 때 — IH 핵심 연결어
방금 한 말을 다시 정리하는 자연스러운 자기수정
곁가지로 샜다가 본론으로 돌아올 때 (담화 관리 = AL 포인트)
하나를 골라야 하거나 의견을 말할 때 시간 벌면서 시작
답변을 깔끔하게 끝낼 때 (침묵으로 끝나는 것보다 훨씬 좋음)

opic.practice_ko: 오늘은 금요일 복습: 세 문항을 쉬지 않고 이어서 녹음(총 5~6분)하고, 이번 주 talk·OPIc 표현을 몇 개 썼는지 체크해 보기. 자기소개는 내 실제 정보로 바꿔 60~90초 안에 끝나게 다듬기.
